title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
grouping: Four borderless columns in one row, each headed by a lettered serif title ((a) Dense Attention ... (d) StreamingLLM (ours)); a column is matrix on top, cache row in the middle, scorecard and a one-line verdict at the bottom. No containers or background tints.
shapes_depth: Each policy is the same lower-triangular attention grid of small square cells: grey for masked or evicted entries, light blue for attended ones, a darker blue diagonal, and a red cell in the bottom-right corner for the current token. Under the grid a horizontal row of KV-cache squares (blue kept, dashed grey outline for evicted, red current token) with curved arrows from the current token to the cached ones and double-headed brackets labelled 'T cached tokens', 'L cached tokens', 'evicted tokens'. Below that a large serif big-O cost and a 'PPL:' value, each followed by a green tick or a red cross and coloured to match.
proposed_highlight: The proposal is the rightmost column with a bold '(ours)' title; it is the only grid with a yellow first column (the kept initial tokens, also yellow in its cache row and pointed to by an 'Attention Sink' callout) and the only column scoring two green ticks.
lesson: Draw every KV-cache policy as the same lower-triangular attention grid (kept cells blue, evicted cells grey) over a matching cache row, and close each column with a cost-and-quality scorecard of green ticks and red crosses, so the proposal is simply the one column with two ticks.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024').

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: streaming LLM inference with KV cache

core.what: four identical panels side by side, (a) dense, (b) window, (c) sliding window with re-computation and (d) StreamingLLM last, each the same attention matrix over the same cache strip with cost and perplexity verdicts beneath

relations.form: four equal panels in one row, ours last with a bold title, each with the same vertical stack: attention matrix, KV-cache strip, O(.) and PPL verdict, one-line summary
each strategy is drawn on a small causal attention matrix (coloured lower-triangle cells) and on a row of cache token squares with evicted tokens dashed and the kept window bracketed with T, T-L or L

in (d) the first few tokens are kept as yellow 'Attention Sink' squares at the left of the cache strip and as a yellow first column in the matrix, separated from the recent window by evicted dashed tokens

channels.colour: blue = attended or cached tokens, grey = tokens not used, red = the current token, yellow = attention-sink tokens (only in ours); in the verdict rows green with a tick = good and red with a cross = bad, so red carries both 'current token' and 'fails'
channels.shape: matrix cells = attention entries; squares in a strip = cached tokens; a dashed outline = an evicted token
channels.line: curved black arrows from the current token to the tokens it attends; double-headed arrows under the strip measure the cache length
channels.frame: none around panels; whitespace and a lettered title separate them

quality.strengths: Identical panels make the four strategies differ only in what changes; the one new idea, keeping initial tokens, is the only new hue (yellow) and appears in both the matrix and the cache; the outcome is placed under each panel in the same position so cost and quality compare across the row.
quality.weaknesses: Red means both the current token and a failed verdict; the curved attention arrows above the cache strips overlap each other in (a) and (b); in (c) the grey upper rows of the matrix are a different idea (truncation) shown with the same grey as 'not attended'.

insights.structure: Four borderless columns, (a) Dense Attention, (b) Window Attention, (c) Sliding Window w/ Re-computation, (d) StreamingLLM (ours), each stacking an attention grid, a KV-cache row, a cost and PPL scorecard, and a one-line verdict.
insights.data: Each policy is the same lower-triangular grid of square cells: grey masked or evicted, light blue attended, dark-blue diagonal, red current token; below it a row of cache squares with dashed grey evicted ones and curved arrows from the current token.
insights.emphasis: The ours column adds a yellow first-column of 'attention sink' cells, and the scorecards use red crosses versus green ticks on O(.) cost and PPL so only (d) gets two ticks.
insights.flow: Left to right across the four alternatives; within a column top to bottom from grid to cache to verdict.

arrangement.units: four unboxed columns under lettered serif titles
arrangement.inputs_as: token cells in the attention grid and cache row
arrangement.shared: identical grid and cache layout reused in every column
